laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are severe and include the death penalty. - Carrying or using drugs
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Surrogacy is illegal in Laos. There have been reports of arrests and charges for human trafficking related to surrogacy. If you're visiting Laos for paid surrogacy or adoption, get legal advice first.
laws.heading: Surrogacy and adoption

laws.rule: Intimate relationships between Lao citizens and foreigners who are not married are illegal. This includes sexual relationships and living together. Marriages between Lao citizens and foreigners must be pre-approved by Lao authorities. This is the case if you are in Laos or another country. Marriage certificates issued outside of Laos need to be checked by a Lao embassy. This needs to happen in the country where the marriage took place. If you don't register a relationship, authorities could fine you or send you to prison.
laws.heading: Intimate relationships

laws.rule: The death penalty can result from serious crimes such as: rape murder drug possession, sale of trafficking treason Activities that are illegal include: taking photos of or visiting military sites making false statements to police wildlife trafficking damaging public property nudity in public or religious places preaching religion, including passing out religious material, without permission visiting temples, other religious or cultural sites after they have closed speaking or publishing material against Laos using, purchasing, possessing, or selling e-cigarettes (vapes), heated tobacco products and shisha, or taking any of these items in or out of Laos, even in transit gambling and playing c
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: In some areas night-time curfews apply after certain hours. Pay close attention to your personal security at all times and follow the instructions from security forces. Curfews may be enforced with short notice or without notice and can include roadblocks, spot roadside checks and occasional raids on premises.
laws.heading: Curfews

laws.rule: To drive, you'll need a valid International Driving Permit (IDP). Australian driver's licences aren't valid. Arrange your IDP before travelling from Australia. - Australian Embassy, Vientiane

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Dress conservatively: tank tops and bikinis are not appropriate in villages or towns, and women in shorts or short skirts must wrap a Lao skirt (sinh) over them before entering temples and other sacred places. Take shoes off before entering a home. Don't touch anyone's head, point with your feet, or sit with your back or feet toward a Buddha image. Women should not sit next to or hand things directly to monks, and don't offer to shake hands with monks. Crouch slightly when passing seated elders. Ask before photographing people, especially children; don't give money or gifts to begging children.
